reasons: The agreement genuinely lacks any post-termination transition or data-return mechanic: Section 13 only shifts re-hosting/name-server burdens onto Client and confirms domain/Content ownership, and Section 14 merely extends service to month-end, so 'missing' is the correct classification for a hosting agreement where TrueLink holds Client borrower and loan data.

The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook model language closely and is adapted to the contract's defined terms (TrueLink, Client, Client Content, Hosting Services, Web Site), covering all three elements: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, and certified deletion thereafter.
The edit is additive only — no existing operative text is altered — which is the minimal intervention needed to reach the preferred position.
The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.

Minor, non-disqualifying points: the inserted heading carries no section number (the rationale calls it 'Section 14a'), and clause (b) is keyed to 'within thirty (30) days of Client's request' rather than of termination — both are cosmetic/negotiable and do not drop the insert below the fallback.
